summary: Horace Hayman Wilson worked in Indology. He held positions at the East India Company, the India Government Mint in Kolkata, the University of Calcutta, Oxford as Boden Professor, the East India Company College, and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Horace L. Friess studied at Columbia and Heidelberg universities, working in religious studies and philosophy. He held a post at Johns Hopkins University and served as a professor at Columbia University from circa 1926 to 1966.
Horst Brinkhaus worked in the field of Indology. He held posts at the University of Münster and at the University of Kiel from circa 1995 to 2011.

Horst Lasic, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD from the University of Vienna around 1993 to 1999. He was a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995) and a Vienna lecturer (1999).

Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim, Cheonghwa, and Steven D. Goodman, completing a Doctor of Philosophy at the California Institute of Integral Studies by 2010.
Houn Jiyu-Kennett worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Durham University and trained under traditional teachers Sek Kim Seng and Keidō Chisan Kohō in the early 1960s.
Hoyo Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University from circa 1952 to 1961 and later served as a professor of Buddhist studies there from circa 1968 to 2004.
Hozen Seki worked in Buddhist studies. He founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church from circa 1938 to 1983.

Hsiang-Kuang Chou worked in sinology and Buddhist studies and studied under Swami Sivananda. He held posts at the University of Allahabad, University of Delhi, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.

Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a PhD at Temple University around 2006. From circa 2007 to 2020, Hu served as associate professor at the University of Detroit Mercy.

Hsing Yun worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at the University of Hong Kong and under Yin Shun. He founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West, and held a post at National Taiwan University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin from circa 2006 to 2009.

Hsu-feng Lee specializes in Buddhist studies. Lee completed a master's degree under Huimin at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney between 2011 and 2017.

Hsuan Hua worked in Buddhist studies and studied under Hsu Yun in 1948. He founded the Buddhist Text Translation Society, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and the Institute for World Religions, serving as abbot at City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

Hsuan-Li Wang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Wang earned a PhD from Columbia University (circa 2008–2015) under supervisor Chun-fang Yu and committee members Bernard Faure, Michael Como, David Max Moerman, and Gray Tuttle.
Hsueh-li Cheng worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaii at Hilo from circa 1974 to 2007.

Hu Shih worked in philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Cornell, Columbia, Teachers College, and National University, and held positions at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Academia Sinica.

Huai-Chin Nan worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy, studied under Huanxian Yuan, and served as a professor of philosophy at Chinese Culture University.

Huaiyu Chen studied under Xinjiang Rong at Peking University and Stephen F. Teiser at Princeton. Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, Chen taught at Rutgers and became assistant professor at Arizona State University around 2007.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held research and academic posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 2009–2011), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (circa 2011–2017), and Zhejiang University (circa 2017).
